page: Microsoft Azure L48as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system allocates 48 dedicated vCPUs spanning 24 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity is provisioned at 384.0 GB of RAM, equating to an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. Cache resources consist of 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Vector extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic instruction support via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Local physical storage is a central architectural feature of the L48as_v4, supplying 11,520 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD capacity. The configuration does not bundle hardware GPUs, relying entirely on CPU-driven compute. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top 25 percent tier for raw compute and concurrency metrics, posting 73,818.26 in stress-ng multi-core testing, 19,783.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 62,728.2 in PassMark CPU score. Memory performance shows strong cached throughput, reaching 3,646.79 GB/sec in small-block read testing, while large-block uncached read and write throughput register in the mid-range at 111.65 GB/sec and 82.84 GB/sec respectively.

Application and synthetic workload results demonstrate strong throughput in high-throughput caching and in-memory key-value environments, achieving 70.18 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Large-scale data ingestion and parallel decompression also perform well, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yielding 269.33 GB/sec. Conversely, large parameter model execution highlights processing boundaries: LLM inference for 70B parameter models drops to 2.53 tokens per second, reflecting the absence of discrete GPU acceleration.

From an infrastructure cost efficiency perspective, bundling over 11 TB of local NVMe SSD storage with high memory capacity reduces the need to configure detached high-IOPS network volumes. The L48as_v4 is suited for large relational databases, distributed NoSQL databases, transactional engines, data indexing nodes, and real-time analytics engines requiring dense local NVMe storage and high multi-core throughput.
description: Microsoft Azure L48as_v4 is a storage-optimized instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz, 384.0 GB of RAM, and 11,520 GB of integrated NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 architecture incorporates AVX-512 vector support and robust cryptographic extensions, while hyper-threading provides 24 physical cores across 48 virtual execution threads without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-threaded processing power, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 19,783.0 and Redis performance reaching 70.18 million operations per second. Memory throughput remains balanced, offering 3,646.79 GB/sec in small-block cached scenarios. By combining 11.5 TB of low-latency local storage with an 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio, the instance provides high density for IOPS-sensitive applications without requiring external premium disk arrays. It is engineered primarily for transactional databases, large NoSQL clusters, real-time log indexing, and distributed data processing pipelines.
